# sdmTMBexperiments

<!-- badges: start -->
[![Lifecycle: experimental](https://img.shields.io/badge/lifecycle-experimental-orange.svg)](https://lifecycle.r-lib.org/articles/stages.html#experimental)
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/DeepWaterIMR/sdmTMBexperiments/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/DeepWaterIMR/sdmTMBexperiments/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
<!-- badges: end -->

**sdmTMBexperiments** is a collection of experimental helper functions for
working with fitted [sdmTMB](https://github.com/sdmTMB/sdmTMB) models: model
comparison, mesh-resolution sensitivity, retrospective analysis,
survey-specific index comparison, prediction-grid construction, and diagnostic
plotting. It doubles as a showcase of how to use these functions and a staging
ground for methods that may later be adopted into `sdmTMB`.

The functions are generic (no species or region is hard-coded) and may be freely
reused — please cite the function developer. Maps are drawn on
[ggOceanMaps](https://mikkovihtakari.github.io/ggOceanMaps/) basemaps, the
package's default map-plotting tool.

## Installation

```r
# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("DeepWaterIMR/sdmTMBexperiments")
```

## Example

```{r example, eval = FALSE}
library(sdmTMBexperiments)
library(sdmTMB)

mesh <- make_mesh(pcod, c("X", "Y"), cutoff = 20)
m1 <- sdmTMB(density ~ 0 + as.factor(year), data = pcod,
             time = "year", mesh = mesh, family = tweedie())
m2 <- sdmTMB(density ~ 0 + as.factor(year) + depth_scaled, data = pcod,
             time = "year", mesh = mesh, family = tweedie())
nd <- replicate_df(qcs_grid, "year", unique(pcod$year))

# Compare two models: indices, spatial prediction differences, Mohn's rho
cmp <- compare_models(m1, m2, newdata = nd, object_crs = 32609)
plot(cmp)
plot(cmp, type = "spatial")

# Retrospective analysis
plot(sdmTMB_retro(m1, nd, nyears = 5))

# Diagnostics
plot_mesh(mesh, crs = 32609, data = pcod, value = "density")
plot_residual_qq(m1)
```

See `vignette("sdmTMBexperiments")` for an end-to-end walkthrough, including
survey comparison with the bundled `sebastes` data.

## Citation

If you use these functions, please cite the package and the function developer
